revision_note: Revision 2, committed before holdout-v2 construction and after the first end-to-end holdout failed. Changes: (1) the repeat-skip safety check now applies only after a run persisted current rows — a review-only or unknown-only first run legitimately runs again; (2) confidence values are no longer asserted because which authority the model cites is not deterministic — routing consistency (high persists claims, medium routes to human review, low stays unknown) is asserted instead; (3) expected outcomes are legal outcome sets (propose and/or insufficient_evidence with preserved unknowns) rather than single outcomes, so evidence-limited advisories can be held honestly. The first end-to-end holdout (SHA256 35c40f9a...) remains frozen and consumed as failure evidence.
applies_to: Phase 6 end-to-end holdout v2 on real public evidence (evaluation correction)
freeze_rule: Committed before holdout-v2 construction. The end-to-end holdout v2 must use real public CVE evidence disjoint from both development datasets and from the consumed first holdout; the complete TypeScript -> Python -> TypeScript -> scratch-database pipeline runs exactly once against it, including receipt, trace, Story/Fact immutability, stale-version, and idempotency checks. A failed or consumed holdout stays immutable; remediation requires a new disjoint holdout. The synthetic normalization fixture holdout (23 cases) and the failed first end-to-end holdout (3 cases) are retained as evidence only and are not gates.
